business_problem: Qdrant needed a scalable and affordable way to offer enterprise-grade vector search for unstructured data so customers could build generative AI and analytics applications without sacrificing low latency or ease of use.
solution_summary: Qdrant hosts its vector search database on AWS as a managed cloud service to help enterprises retrieve information from unstructured data for generative AI and analytics use cases. The platform indexes private data as vectors so ML and AI teams can run low-latency similarity queries for conversational search, facial recognition, anomaly detection, product recommendations, and other workloads. The commercial managed version launched on AWS in 2023 alongside its open-source offering and is distributed through AWS Marketplace, giving cloud adopters a preferred deployment option. By relying on fully managed AWS storage and compute infrastructure rather than operating everything itself, Qdrant can scale its database more easily and cut total resource costs by more than 30 percent while keeping performance and ease of use high.
data_flow: Enterprise unstructured data is indexed in Qdrant's managed vector database on AWS, queried through low-latency similarity search, and returned to AI and analytics applications that need conversational retrieval or other vector-search capabilities.
business_outcome: Qdrant gives enterprises a managed AWS-hosted vector database for conversational retrieval and other unstructured-data use cases, while reducing its own total resource costs by more than 30 percent through fully managed AWS infrastructure.
metrics: saved more than 30 percent in total costs
